sentences: This is FaithGuard.
It checks AI answers about company annual reports, before they reach the reader.
More and more people ask AI assistants about financial reports.
The answers sound confident, but the numbers are not always right.
A figure can look right and still be wrong: miscalculated, read at the wrong scale, or taken from the wrong part of the report.
In our benchmark, most errors were simply wrong numbers; wrong-context ones were rare.
One wrong figure can mislead an investment or an audit decision.
These mistakes are hard to catch: you must find the right line, and often redo the arithmetic.
And for Sri Lankan companies, we found no comparable public dataset to test this.
FaithGuard works in three steps.
First, it detects. Every number in the answer is checked against the report's own tables. Numbers that do not match are flagged, with the reason, but some errors are missed.
Second, it decides: should the answer be sent as it is, repaired, or held back?
Third, it repairs. Flagged numbers are replaced with the report's own figures, so every changed number can be traced to its source.
And if an answer is held back, the reader gets the evidence and an honest explanation instead.
Here, FaithGuard sees that the profit figure belongs to the Bank.
It swaps in the Group's figure, recalculates the growth, and shows exactly where each number came from.
What makes FaithGuard different?
It trains a detector on context mistakes built from US company filings, though our tests have not shown that this helps.
It fixes numbers precisely, instead of rewriting whole answers.
It tests a limit on how many wrong answers get through, and says so when the limit cannot be met.
It runs on small, open models and free hardware.
And it comes with a new benchmark of Sri Lankan and US annual reports.
Three parts, one goal: detection, decision and repair.
FaithGuard: the right number, in the right context.
